I did not swap the target for you because building for a different architecture changes your goal.

explained: SA_RESTART is not supported on QNX SDP 8.0, so this cannot be fixed by changing flags or environment. The SDP's own header comments the definition out: $QNX_TARGET/usr/include/signal.h line 163 reads '/* #define SA_RESTART 0x0040 (not supported yet) */'. Adding -D or a feature-test macro will not help, and defining SA_RESTART yourself (for example as 0) would compile, but interrupted kernel calls would still fail with EINTR instead of restarting. That would silently change what the program does, so I'm not applying it. The supported approach is to edit sig.c: remove SA_RESTART from sa.sa_flags (use 0 or other supported SA_* flags), and wrap any blocking calls (read, write, waitpid, and so on) in a retry loop such as 'while ((r = read(...)) == -1 && errno == EINTR);'. If the code must also build on other platforms, guard it with '#ifdef SA_RESTART'. After that, 'qcc -Vgcc_ntox86_64 -o sig sig.c' should build.

(2) Keep 64-bit ARM and switch to an emulator that supports it, for example QEMU: mkqnximage --type=qemu --arch=aarch64le --ssh-ident=none --noprompt.
Tell me which you want and I'll help get that build working.

explained: Architecture mismatch, and none of the available fix actions can solve it. `file hello` reports `ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64 ... interpreter /usr/lib/ldqnx-64.so.2`. But qnx-doctor-target-run always boots an x86_64 image (`mkqnximage --type=qemu --arch=x86_64`). The x86_64 kernel can't exec an aarch64 ELF, so ksh fell back to reading it as a shell script. That is why the output shows the garbage `ELF��@` line, then 'cannot execute - No such file or directory', then 'no closing quote'. Nothing is wrong with the SDP environment or the runner. The binary was simply built for the wrong target. To fix it, rebuild hello for x86_64 with the SDP compiler: `qcc -Vgcc_ntox86_64 -o hello hello.c` (or `x86_64-pc-nto-qnx8.0.0-gcc`, or `-Vgcc_ntox86_64` in your Makefile). Then re-run `qnx-doctor-target-run ./hello`. If you need to test the aarch64 build, you would need an aarch64 target or image instead, such as real hardware or `mkqnximage --arch=aarch64le`. This runner doesn't provide that.
